# Epic: Option A — status-neutral assignee CAS claim for the audit tier + remove `needsProducerReview`

## Problem statement

When the herdr downtime worker auto-dispatches an audit of a completed/in_review item, its CAS claim flips `status` to `in_progress` while leaving the stage at `in_review`, creating a hybrid `in-progress`/`in_review` pair that the audit runner's failure-restore path cannot represent — so a failed audit (Phase 2 timeout, infra failure, killed pane) coerces the item to `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, stranding it off the review queue (root cause: WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL). Separately, `needsProducerReview` has grown into a magic DB flag whose two roles — blocking auto-dispatch and gating the ship release — need to be re-homed onto the assignee field so the flag and its whole surface (`wl reviewed`, CLI/API filters, herdr icon/logic, audit runner, ship gate) can be removed.

## Users

- **Operator** running herdr downtime dispatch. Story: "When an auto-dispatched audit of a completed/in_review item fails, I want the item to stay completed/in_review — on the review queue and re-selectable — so broken audits never strand work in in-progress/plan_complete."
- **Producer** reviewing work. Story: "I want an explicit, per-item way to pause automatic scheduling (assign the item to me) that does not rely on a magic DB flag, and I want a release gate that still stops me from shipping unreviewed work."
- **Agent tier / pane** competing for the same item. Story: "Exactly one concurrent claim must win, even when the claim does not change status."

## Approach (Option A, per root cause fix-options)

Make the audit-tier claim **status-neutral**: the claim's CAS becomes the **assignee** instead of `status`. Add `--if-assignee <value>` to `wl update` (atomic `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` CAS, same machinery as `updateIfMatches`), then the audit-tier claim writes:

```
wl update <id> --assignee <agent> --if-status completed --if-stage in_review --if-assignee ""
```

The item stays completed/in_review throughout — no hybrid state is ever created, so the audit runner's pre-audit capture and failure-restore are correct (no `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` coercion to plan_complete). Exactly one pane still wins (CAS on the guarded fields), preserving the WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT RC-1 single-claim guarantee.

Remove `needsProducerReview` from the database and re-home its two roles onto the assignee field:
- **Scheduling hold:** assign to the producer ⇒ no tier claims it ⇒ no auto-dispatch.
- **Release gate:** an item assigned to the producer means "the producer owns it"; `check-final-validation.js` blocks release until such items have been reviewed (audit verdict 'Ready to close: Yes').

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl update` supports `--if-assignee` CAS (atomic, single-winner; unit + integration tests).
- [ ] Audit-tier claim is status-neutral: item stays completed/in_review through dispatch and failed-audit restore (`wl show` after simulated failure shows completed/in_review).
- [ ] Regression test: herdr dispatch claim → simulated audit Phase-2 failure → item back at completed/in_review, re-selectable (no in-progress/plan_complete, no needsProducerReview-column dependency).
- [ ] Failed dispatch (marker-write-failed / spawn-failed) clears assignee and leaves item re-selectable.
- [ ] Success path clears assignee; legacy residue cleared by a one-time migration/script; audit re-runs still dispatch.
- [ ] Assign item to producer ⇒ no tier auto-dispatches it (claims fail stale at every tier) — the scheduling hold works.
- [ ] `needsProducerReview` column removed from DB; `wl reviewed` and all `--needs-producer-review` CLI/API options removed; no references left in src/, packages/, skill/, .pi/skills/.
- [ ] Ship release gate re-homed onto the assignee hold without weakening release safety (check-final-validation.js updated + tested).
- [ ] Sync regression guard behaviour for assignee documented/decided and tested cross-root.
- [ ] Full test suite passes; CLI.md / docs updated; AGENTS.md claim pattern updated.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo skill boundary:** `audit_runner.py`, `status_lifecycle.py`, and the ship gate scripts (`check-final-validation.js`, `check-audit-gate.js`, `run-release.js`) live in the **SorraAgents** skill tree (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`). AGENTS.md forbids editing `skill/` dirs without explicit instruction; changes there must be tracked as SA work items linked from here (see bug intake question 2 — repo boundary, still awaiting producer answer).
- **No hybrid status/stage write:** the new claim path must never produce `in-progress`/`in_review`; the old dual-set claim is the bug's source.
- **Race safety preserved:** the `--if-assignee ""` guard is the exclusive token; rollback must be similarly guarded (`--if-assignee <agent>`) so only this claim's state is reverted.
- **Assignee residue is a live problem:** 698 completed items and 7 in_review items already carry `assignee=Map` (P1); the legacy-cleanup is table-stakes or the queue ossifies.
- **Sync regression guard:** `assignee` is merge-participating and `'Map' → ''` is refused as a regression on other roots unless the guard is changed or `--accept-regressions` used (P3).
- **Migration history preserved:** the add-migration (20260210-add-needsProducerReview) stays for history; a new drop-migration removes the column.
- **Docs/conventions:** AGENTS.md claim pattern, herdr README downtime-dispatcher docs, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md, CLI.md, icons-design.md, CHANGELOG updated.
- **UK English, Markdown descriptions, wl is source of truth** per project rules.
- **Push only to `dev`** per push policy.

## Existing state

- `wl update` supports `--if-status` / `--if-stage` CAS (used by `claimWorkItem` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`, which flips `--status in_progress --assignee <agent>`); no `--if-assignee` field exists yet.
- `claimWorkItem` (fetcher.ts:1197) and `rollbackClaimWorkItem` (fetcher.ts:1268) implement the dispatch claim/rollback; `downtime-worker.ts` (`dispatchClaimedTier`, `rollbackClaimForFailure`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, all `select*` functions) consumes them.
- `needsProducerReview` is stored in the DB (column, migration 20260210-add-needsProducerReview), exposed via `wl reviewed` (src/commands/reviewed.ts), `wl update --needs-producer-review`, `wl list/search/next` filters, api.ts query param, cli-types, persistent-store schema/jsonl/sync.
- The audit runner (SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets `--needs-producer-review yes` on 'yes' verdicts and never clears `--assignee ""` (P1). Its failure-restore path has an inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` that coerces `in_review → plan_complete`.
- The ship release gate (`skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js`) blocks release on `needsProducerReview === true` items.
- `interview.ts` explains/clears the flag (P5); github.js `--add-assignee` and delegate-helper write `assignee=@github-copilot` (P6).

## Desired change

- Add `--if-assignee` CAS to `wl update` (atomic single-winner).
- herdr audit-tier claim becomes status-neutral (assignee CAS against `""`); dispatch rollback clears assignee guarded on `--if-assignee <agent>`; audit runner clears assignee on every terminal verdict path (success 'yes', failure restore, verdict 'no').
- Define the scheduling-hold convention: non-empty assignee = item intentionally held from auto-dispatch (assign → producer ⇒ hold). All skills clear assignee on session end (status_lifecycle failure-exit already does; intake/delegate/triage reviewed).
- One-time legacy cleanup of assignee residue (698+ items).
- Drop `needsProducerReview` everywhere: migration, persistent-store/sync/jsonl, CLI/API (`wl reviewed`, filters, query params, cli-types), herdr (grouping, icons, pane-lifecycle, pane-close*, stalled-work, settings, fetcher, downtime-worker select*/classify), theme.ts, interview.ts, audit runner ('yes' verdict path), ship check-final-validation.js (re-homed onto assignee hold), docs.
- Sync regression guard handled per open question Q1.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — add `--if-assignee` CAS (normalizeActionArgs + update path)
- `src/persistent-store.ts` / `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `updateIfMatches`/CAS field surface, column removal, schema/CRUD
- `src/sync.ts` — merge-participating/regression-guard behaviour for `assignee` (Q1)
- `src/commands/reviewed.ts` — remove/repurpose the command
- `src/commands/list.ts`, `src/commands/search.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`, `src/commands/create.ts`, `src/api.ts`, `src/cli-types.ts` — remove `--needs-producer-review` options/param
- `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`, `src/theme.ts` — producer-review icon/flags
- `src/commands/interview.ts` — flag explain/clear flow (replace or update)
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — drop-column migration
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — status-neutral `claimWorkItem` + guarded `rollbackClaimWorkItem` (+ `--if-assignee`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatch claim/rollback/select*/classifyItemForDispatch (filtering moves to assignee-based)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`, pane-lifecycle/stalled-work/settings — `needsProducerReview` icon/logic removal
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents) — clear assignee on terminal verdicts; 'yes' verdict producer-hold
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents) — assignee-clear conventions (already on failure)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` (SorraAgents) — release gate re-homed onto assignee hold (+ `check-audit-gate.js`, `run-release.js`)
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`, `tests/cli/*`, `tests/unit/*`, migration tests
- Docs: `AGENTS.md` (both repos), `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/icons-design.md`

## Related work

- WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL — root cause bug (depends-on blocker of this epic; its intake interview on fix approach + repo boundary is awaiting producer answers)
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — RCA: downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (CAS claim design point 1; RC-1 single-claim guarantee this epic must preserve)
- WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH — downtime dispatcher hard-strikes on retired 'in_progress' stage (retired-stage `migrateStage` claim path in fetcher.ts)
- WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A — cross-root coordination offers (per-call `--worklog-dir` claim targeting; P3 cross-root concern)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R — herdr: flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale
- WL-0MU72WJ8C0005GIE — herdr dispatcher ignores needsProducerReview on live dispatch path
- WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F — downtime dispatcher excludes items needing producer review from selection
- WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE — critical items always progress first (dispatch ordering)
- WL-0MT32F908002YFFA — recover items stranded by marker-write-failed / spawn-failed
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 — herdr audit tier re-checks for fresh audit after selection
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN — conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion
- SA side (SorraAgents): audit runner items, ship gate items (linked during planning)

## Out of scope

- Option B (audit_runner `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` addition) — keep as fallback if Option A is blocked; the bug's intake recommends a staged interim audit-runner fix (Option B as a small SA-side item first), which is tracked on the root-cause bug, not here.
- Changing the implement/plan/intake tiers' status flip (they are legitimately in_progress while worked).

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Assignee-hold convention breaks existing flows.** Any skill that leaves a non-empty assignee (intake, implement, triage, delegate `@github-copilot`) silently suppresses future auto-dispatch. Mitigation: audit every assignee writer, clear on session end (status_lifecycle failure-exit already does), document in AGENTS.md, and add a test that a cleared claim re-enables dispatch.
- **R2 — Legacy residue cleanup could strand live items.** The one-time cleanup of 698 completed + 7 in_review assigned items must run after the code change ships, be idempotent, and scope to audit-hold residue only (not e.g. in-flight implement claims).
- **R3 — Release-gate weakening.** Re-homing the ship gate onto the assignee hold must not make unreviewed items shippable. Mitigation: gate checks producer-assigned items for a passing audit ('Ready to close: Yes') before closeWorkItemsAfterRelease.
- **R4 — Cross-repo coordination.** Skill-side changes (audit_runner, status_lifecycle, ship gate) live in SorraAgents; if they are not tracked/implemented via SA work items, the epic's AC "no references left" cannot be met. Assumed: SA items are created during planning (pending the bug's repo-boundary answer).
- **R5 — Sync regression guard fights assignee clearing** (P3) and **R6 — `--if-assignee` needs full CAS semantics** (atomic `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, mirrors `--if-status`/`--if-stage`; introduced in `wl update` only, not other commands) — both captured in ACs (9 and 1).

## Open questions (Appendix)

- Q1 (sync regression guard, P3): (a) treat `assignee` as a normal non-regression-guarded merge field so `''` clears propagate cross-root, or (b) accept `assignee` as an owned reconciliation field and document the cross-root rule? **Recommended: (a)** — the status-neutral claim's whole point is that the cleared assignee must propagate so the item is re-selectable everywhere; a regression-guarded assignee resurrects claims across panes/roots and would need `--accept-regressions` noise on every sync. **ACCEPTED — option (a), implemented and tested in WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ (C3).** `assignee` is removed from the regression-guard merge-participating fields in `src/sync.ts` and its empty value is treated as meaningful intent (`isEmptyMeaningfulField`), so a newer remote `''` clears a local non-empty assignee and propagates cross-root without `--accept-regressions` (last-writer-wins by `updatedAt`; deterministic tie-break at equal timestamps). Status/stage/priority remain guarded. Coverage: `tests/cli/sync-assignee-clear.test.ts` (two roots, real `wl sync`) and unit tests in `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts`.
- Q2 (producer-hold assignee value, P5/P7): what literal value marks the producer hold (e.g. operator identity `rog`, a reserved `producer` sentinel, or `@github-copilot`-style)? **Recommended: a reserved well-known value equal to the producer's wl identity used by the release gate** so the hold is self-describing; exact value to be confirmed with the producer. **OPEN QUESTION — record the operator's identity during planning.**
- Q3 (dependency direction): this epic currently holds `depends-on` → WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL (the root-cause bug it resolves), leaving it `blocked`. Confirm this is intentional sequencing (bug root-cause decided first) vs. the epic superseding the bug. **Recommended: keep depends-on on the root cause until its intake decision lands, then have the epic's completion close the bug as fixed-by (recorded as related work; direction reviewed at planning).** **OPEN QUESTION — traceability reviewed during planning.**

*Source: repository inspection (fetcher.ts, downtime-worker.ts, sync.ts, reviewed.ts, interview.ts, migrations, SorraAgents skill tree), bug intake records, and work-item history. No interactive interview conducted — herdr-dispatched session; seed context was exhaustive.*

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKRRZ2DN1B8MKZS** – Implement next command (completed)
- **WL-0MRJ3TUPP002TSGI** – Change in_review icons and reuse audit column for requiresProducerReview flag (completed)
- **WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV** – Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msrbffln005w3vt, 0mtq14w7l003ii5a, accept, acceptance, add (+300 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mtq14w7l003ii5a, accept, add, addition, agent (+270 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: accept, add, added, addition, agent (+232 more)

# Herdr selection list: `Blocked By` metadata line flickers endlessly on blocked items (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP)

**Headline:** The Herdr metadata panel has two live render states for a blocked item (async `Blocked By` lookup pending → line absent; resolved → line present), and `doRefresh()` clears the per-item blocker cache on *every* list refresh, so frequent refresh triggers (DB-change watch, auto-sync counter bumps, `wl next` re-sorts) re-flip the panel between the two states endlessly. Fix: make the resolved state survive refreshes and invalidate only when the item's dependency edges can actually change.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, selecting a dependency-blocked item makes the metadata panel's `Blocked By` line appear for a moment, then disappear for a moment, then reappear — repeating endlessly. Selecting a blocked item is therefore visually noisy and leaves the "what is this blocked on?" answer (added by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8) unreliable at a glance.

## RCA (root cause analysis)

There are two distinct render states for the work-item preview, and the live loop flips between them on every refresh:

- **Path A — metadata panel, resolved:** `formatMetadataPanel(..., metaBlockedBy)` renders one `Blocked By` row per active blocker. `metaBlockedBy` is produced by `resolveMetaBlockers()` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), which resolves asynchronously via `fetchBlockersForItem()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`; spawns `wl dep list <id> --json` plus one `wl show` per candidate blocker) and caches the result in an in-memory `blockerCache` keyed by item ID.
- **Path B — metadata panel, unresolved:** until the lookup lands (or after the cache is dropped), `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined`, `state.metaBlockedBy` is `null`, and the panel renders **without** the `Blocked By` rows. A follow-up `render()` is scheduled from the fetch's `.finally()`, so the line pops in ~one lookup latency later (~0.5–2 s for two spawned `wl` processes).

**Why it repeats endlessly:** `doRefresh()` calls `blockerCache.clear()` on **every** list refresh (`worklist.ts`, in the refresh path). Every cache clear re-introduces the unresolved frame for the full async lookup, then the `.finally(render())` flips it back. Refreshes fire far more often than the 30 s tick in a live workspace:

- the DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) reacts within ~150 ms (debounce) to any `wl` state-counter bump — real agent writes, and *every successful auto-sync* (`src/commands/sync.ts` bumps the read-cache counter) — each feeding `requestWatchRefresh → doRefresh`;
- the auto-sync task itself runs `doRefresh(false)` unconditionally on its cadence;
- `wl next` re-sorts bump the counter when the dispatcher runs it (`src/commands/next.ts`).

So under sustained write/sync traffic the line alternates on/off continuously — the reported "for a moment… disappear for a moment… repeat endlessly". The design intent ("an unresolved item renders without rows and a follow-up render shows them") assumed a one-time transition per selection; invalidating the cache on every refresh breaks that assumption.

**Secondary inconsistency (the "other path" the report refers to):** only the list-mode metadata panel renders `Blocked By`. The **detail view** (`formatDetailContent`, the other work-item preview render path) builds its metadata table from `buildMetaRows()` without blocker rows, and the hover tooltip (`formatTooltipLines`) also omits them — so the two preview render paths have already diverged (one has the line, the other does not).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** browsing the Herdr selection list. Story: "When I select a blocked item, I want the `Blocked By` line to appear once and stay put until the data actually changes — not flash on and off."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Selecting a dependency-blocked item shows the `Blocked By` line stably: once resolved, no render frame drops the line on subsequent auto-refresh ticks, DB-change (watcher) refreshes, or auto-sync cycles; observed over ≥3 consecutive refresh cycles with the DB otherwise idle.
- [ ] List refreshes never blank the panel: a refresh reuses the last known blockers for the same selected item (or resolves from the freshly fetched payload) instead of re-running the async lookup and rendering an unresolved frame; there is at most one spawn of `wl dep list` (and enrichment) per item until its edges can actually change (selection change, or a refresh that changed the item's dependency set).
- [ ] The live loop is bounded and self-terminating: a blocked item under simulated refresh + counter/watch events ends in a stable frame set (exactly one unresolved→resolved transition per selection), never an oscillating pair.
- [ ] Unblocked items are unaffected: their metadata panel output is byte-for-byte unchanged; headings, list navigation, description preview, and `m`/`M` scroll clamping (including `metadataPanelContentHeight` with `metaBlockedBy`) behave as before.
- [ ] The two preview render paths are reconciled: the detail view either renders the same `Blocked By` rows as the list metadata panel, or this divergence is explicitly documented out of scope with a code comment — but the report's "two paths, one has the line, one does not" inconsistency must be resolved one way or the other.
- [ ] Fail-open behaviour is preserved: a failed `wl dep list`/`wl show` still yields no `Blocked By` rows and never breaks rendering or navigation.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: stable frames across repeated refreshes for a blocked selection; single-flight/no re-spawn for an unchanged selection; cache reuse semantics; and the detail-view parity decision.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Display-only change**: the fix must not create or mutate dependency edges, and must not change list-data shape for non-panel consumers.
- **Render path must never block**: keep synchronous rendering; any resolution stays async but never causes a visual regression to an earlier frame.
- **Reuse existing helpers**: `isActiveBlocker()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`) and `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
- **No extra `wl` spawns on refresh**: refresh must not re-run the per-item blocker lookup when nothing about that item's edges changed.
- **Scope**: primary fix is the selection-list metadata panel flicker. Detail-view/tooltip parity is secondary and decided within this item (fix or explicitly documented out of scope).

## Existing state

- `resolveMetaBlockers` + `blockerCache`/`blockerInFlight` (async, per-selection, cached by item ID, cleared in `doRefresh`) — introduced by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8.
- `formatMetadataPanel`/`buildMetadataPanelLines` render `Blocked By` rows from the `blockedBy` argument; `metadataPanelContentHeight` shares the same content so the scroll clamp matches the renderer (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8).
- The DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) deliberately watches only the state-counter file to avoid the WAL/`-shm` self-sustaining loop (WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN); the counter is bumped by every `wl` write, successful `wl sync`, and `wl next` re-sort byproduct (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`) — the refresh triggers that drive the flicker cadence.
- Loop-free refresh machinery (single-flight + trailing coalescing in `doRefresh`, debounced `requestWatchRefresh`, scheduler at `scheduler.ts`) is in place and must be preserved.

## Desired change

Make the `Blocked By` state transition idempotent and non-regressive per selection:

1. Keep the renderer's two states (with/without rows) but stop re-clearing the cache on unrelated refreshes — invalidate only when the selected item's dependency edges can have changed (new selection, or a refresh that changes the item), or resolve blockers from the fresh payload so the resolved state survives refresh atomically.
2. Cache the in-flight lookup itself so repeated refreshes never race/duplicate the spawn, and re-render from cache thereafter.
3. Decide and implement detail-view parity (render the same rows or document the divergence).

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`, render-loop wiring of `metaBlockedBy`; `formatDetailContent`/`formatTooltipLines` for parity.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchBlockersForItem` (lookup + per-edge enrichment); consider promise-level memoisation.
- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts` — the refresh triggers whose counter bumps set the flicker cadence (context; not expected to change).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-blockers.test.ts` — regression tests.

## Related work

- WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8 — "Show what an item is blocked on": parent feature that introduced the flickering async render path (regression source).
- WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN — "…DB-change watch" producer-rejection fix: the loop-free state-counter contract any fix must respect.
- WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA / WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W — read-cache + sync-heartbeat work that bumps the counter on sync (refresh frequency context).
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — prior "momentary collapse on refresh (flicker)" bug: the refresh path must stay atomic.
- WL-0MT9ZJF28004UJ28 — description-preview caching in the same metadata panel (precedent for cache-invalidation semantics).

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MT1JH1HN004JP1F** – T5: Metadata panel group info on heading (completed)
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)

Repository file matches: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (keyword overlap only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reported flicker is the list-mode metadata panel alternating between the unresolved and resolved `Blocked By` frames on repeated refreshes; the "two paths" wording also matches the detail view missing the line. Both readings are covered in the ACs.
- **Assumption:** refreshes in the reporter's environment were frequent enough (live workspace with agent writes / auto-sync / dispatcher `wl next`) to make the per-refresh blanking look continuous. The fix must be robust even under a fast refresh loop.
- **Risk — over-invalidation fix:** caching forever can show stale blockers after a real dependency change; the invalidation rule must distinguish "nothing changed" (reuse) from "item changed" (re-resolve).
- **Risk — spawn amplification:** the current code already spawns `wl dep list` + up to N× `wl show` per lookup; the fix must not add spawns to the refresh path.
- **Scope-creep risk:** detail-view/tooltip parity is tempting to expand; keep it to fix-or-document per AC5. Extra ideas should be tracked as separate work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed report plus repository investigation were sufficient to define the problem and the measurable acceptance criteria.

- Q (implicit): "Which code path renders the `Blocked By` line, and why does it flicker?" — Answer (investigation): two live states in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined` while the async `fetchBlockersForItem()` lookup is pending (line absent) and the cached array once it lands (line present); `doRefresh()` clears `blockerCache` on every refresh, so each refresh re-enters the absent state. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (`fetchBlockersForItem`).
- Q (implicit): "Do the two preview render paths differ?" — Answer (investigation): yes — list-mode `formatMetadataPanel` renders `Blocked By`; the detail view `formatDetailContent` (and the hover tooltip `formatTooltipLines`) build metadata from `buildMetaRows()` only and omit it. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q (implicit): "What sets the flicker cadence?" — Answer (investigation + empirical check): the DB-change watch/react + auto-sync (successful `wl sync` bumps the read-cache state counter) + `wl next` re-sort byproduct bumps; verified with `wl list`/`wl show`/`wl dep list --json` that plain reads do not bump the counter. Source: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`.
